subject: Surge coverage matrix and deal prioritization — US / EU / APAC
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Surge coverage matrix draft + asks for prioritization

Hannah / team —

Following up from the QBR: attached is a first-pass "surge coverage" matrix that maps incoming deal triggers to the minimal and preferred node allocations across US / EU / APAC. This is focused on the three live deals that could require immediate tri-region capacity in Q4, the largest being Cerebra Labs (deal attached).

Ask: can we triage which namespace(s) we are comfortable reserving burst vs sustained capacity for? The matrix includes three options per region:
- Option A: minimal burst only (saves ~45% cost)
- Option B: balanced burst + sustain (preferred for performance-sensitive LLMs)
- Option C: dedicated sustained pool (SLA-backed)

Key notes:
- Cerebra expects an APAC-first rollout but legal prefers EU data residency for subset of traffic.
- We currently have limited spare nodes in EU for GPU families that support INT8 quant stacks — that constrains Option B/C sizing.

Attachments: surge_matrix_v1.csv, deal_summary_Cerebra.pdf

Next steps (suggested):
1) Hannah to confirm prioritization order (APAC/EU/US?) for Cerebra.
2) Karthik to propose concrete node counts for each option (per region).
3) Ben to run mid-month cost delta if we shift from A->B for the EU cluster.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Surge coverage matrix draft + asks for prioritization

Vanessa — thanks, good concise framing. A few immediate asks:

- Prioritize APAC (Singapore) for Cerebra's initial ramp but carve an EU-compliant path (Frankfurt) for the residency subset. If resource constraints force a trade, accept burst in APAC and sustained in EU for Phase 1.
- Karthik: can you model two concrete tilings: a conservative (A->B by ramp) and an aggressive (B->C immediate) with token-per-second assumptions and expected Q4 TPS peaks?
- Ben: include a simple NPV on the three options for the first 6 months (capex/opex delta).

We should aim to lock a recommended plan by EOD Monday so Vanessa can take it into procurement discussions with Cerebra.

— Hannah
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

On Fri, Sep 3, 2027 at 11:04 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Karthik: can you model two concrete tilings: a conservative (A->B by ramp) and an aggressive (B->C immediate) with token-per-second assumptions and expected Q4 TPS peaks?

Attached: cost_runup_q4.xlsx (tabbed: assumptions, conservative_tiling, aggressive_tiling). High-level summary here:

Conservative (A->B):
- APAC: start with 6 burst nodes (T4x2 equiv), scale to 12 sustained over 6 weeks.
- EU: start with 4 burst nodes, scale to 8 sustained over 8 weeks (data residency subset pinned to these).
- US: maintain existing baseline, add 4 burst nodes for redundancy.

Aggressive (B->C immediate):
- APAC: 18 sustained nodes (to cover peak + 20% buffer).
- EU: 12 sustained nodes (data residency + buffer).
- US: 8 sustained nodes for multi-region failover.

Estimated impact (6-month run rate):
- Conservative: +$420k incremental run-rate (net of expected discounts).
- Aggressive: +$1.28M incremental run-rate.

Notes / constraints:
- EU inventory for INT8-compatible nodes will be tight; if Cerebra insists on EU sustained for larger volumes we need a 4–6 week lead time to source hardware or provide a cross-region fallback with encrypted KV cache.

I can convert these into the surge coverage matrix by Monday; let me know if you want different cost granularity.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Hannah —

Thanks for the plan and the options. Quick clarifications from product/procurement POV:
- APAC-first is correct (SG) — we will route 70% of early traffic there.
- EU-residency applies to our EU customers only (~12% of traffic) and must be served from EU-sited nodes.
- Time constraint: we need Phase 1 live by 2027-11-15 for a regional pilot. That narrows our preferred approach to Conservative (A->B) unless you can guarantee sourcing for aggressive within 5 weeks.

Procurement: can we get an estimated SOW + lead time for EU node procurement? Also please provide the support SLA delta between Option B and Option C.

Sam Cho
